about.title: Personal Injury Help in Folsom, California
about.longDescription: Folsom sits along the American River at the eastern edge of Sacramento County, a city of about 76,000 people whose daily traffic funnels through a handful of arterials. Public-record collision counts for 2025 show 80 injury collisions here, with 113 people hurt and 6 lives lost. The corridors that appear most often in those records are E Bidwell Street, Iron Point Road, Blue Ravine Road, and Riley Street, and reported crashes tend to peak on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when commuters are heading home. Behind each of those numbers is a person suddenly dealing with pain, paperwork, and an insurance adjuster who is not on their side. That is where we come in. We handle personal injury claims in Folsom and throughout Sacramento County. Our team works on contingency, meaning you pay no fee unless there is a recovery. Whether you were rear-ended on the way to Folsom Lake, bitten by a dog on a neighborhood walk, or injured in a fall at a store, a conversation costs you nothing.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Folsom Claim

items.title: Two years to act — sometimes far less
items.desc: California gives most injury claims a two-year filing window, but a claim against a city, county, or state agency may need to be filed within six months. Starting early protects your options.

items.title: Partial fault won't shut you out
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault. If you share some blame for a crash on Iron Point Road, your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than erased.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not limit non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress, or loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency. You don't pay attorney fees out of pocket, and nothing is owed unless your case results in a recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Folsom?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. If a government entity is involved — for example, a city vehicle or a hazard on public property — the claim deadline can be as short as six months. Because those windows differ, it helps to speak with us sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do collisions in Folsom tend to be reported?
items.answer: Public collision records for 2025 list E Bidwell Street, Iron Point Road, Blue Ravine Road, and Riley Street as the corridors with the highest counts. Those same records show crashes peaking on Wednesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m. These are neutral counts that reflect where and when traffic volume is heaviest, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by whatever share of fault is assigned to you, but you are not barred from recovering. For instance, someone found 30 percent responsible can still recover the remaining 70 percent of their damages.

items.question: What will it cost me to talk to you?
items.answer: Our consultation is free, and we work on contingency. That means no fees unless there is a recovery in your case. You can discuss your situation without worrying about an upfront bill.
